title: Rectal adenocarcinoma
subtitle: Neoadjuvant chemoradiation is the hallmark deviation from the colon strategy — metastatic regimens are otherwise the same. Staging, prognosis and most systemic therapy defer to the colon page
source: Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Rectal Cancer (Tam AY, Shaheen S) · NCCN · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Colonoscopy + biopsy with MMR / MSI testing and pathology review
MRI pelvis (3T) — the rectal-specific study; rectal ultrasound if MRI contraindicated, inconclusive, or for superficial lesions
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis · FDG-PET if potentially curable M1
PIK3CA testing in stage II–III — if mutated, aspirin 100–162 mg daily × 3 years post-op
If metastatic: KRAS, BRAF, HER2, POLE/POLD1, RET, NTRK
Genetics referral for all rectal cancer <50 y, or a somatic finding with germline implications

blocks.heading: Risk definitions
rows: cT4a or cT4b · extramural vascular invasion · cN2 · involved mesorectal fascia · enlarged lateral nodes considered metastatic
positive margins · lymphovascular invasion · poorly differentiated · submucosal invasion to the lower third
direct extension through serosa into prostate, seminal vesicles, cervix or vagina
blocks.footnote: TNM is otherwise identical to colon — see the colon one-pager for stage groups and for all metastatic systemic therapy.

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: RT-sparing: FOLFOX/CAPEOX × 12–16 wk with radiation reserved for inadequate regression
short-course RT + chemo TNT: pCR 28% vs 14%; lower distant relapse but possible higher local recurrence (Dijkstra, Ann Surg 2023)
watch-and-wait after clinical CR to TNT preserves the organ without compromising survival
dostarlimab in dMMR rectal cancer — basis for immunotherapy over TNT
ongoing — RT omission and course length

blocks.html:
Watch-and-wait requires a complete clinical response on all three of DRE, rectal MRI, and direct endoscopic evaluation — and only in centers with experienced multidisciplinary teams, after careful discussion with the patient.

RAPIDO caveat: short-course RT lowered distant relapse but may raise local recurrence, so high-risk patients get TNT as induction chemo followed by chemoradiation. Short-course candidacy is a multidisciplinary decision weighing downstaging against long-term toxicity.

boxes: driven by the RAPIDO local-recurrence signal
add RT only if regression inadequate
if clinical CR: watch and wait (see note)
up to 6 months; reassess every 2–3 months

blocks.heading: Regimens & dosing
rows: 5-FU 225 mg/m² IV over 24 h, 5 days per week
capecitabine 825 mg/m² PO BID on days of radiation
500 mg IV × 4 doses, then 1000 mg IV
240 mg (or 3 mg/kg if <40 kg) · or 480 mg
nivo 3 mg/kg + ipi 1 mg/kg × 4, then nivo maintenance
named only here — dosing on the colon page

blocks.heading: Biomarker → therapy
rows: Neoadjuvant/definitive immunotherapy up to 6 months — preferred over TNT; dostarlimab, nivolumab or pembrolizumab
ICI preferred if no prior exposure: nivolumab ± ipilimumab, pembrolizumab, dostarlimab, cemiplimab, retifanlimab, toripalimab, tislelizumab
Aspirin 100–162 mg daily × 3 years after surgery
Prognostic only — not for treatment decisions outside a trial

blocks.heading: Surveillance
items: Same as colon cancer for stage I–IV, except after transanal local excision
Transanal local excision: proctoscopy (with EUS or MRI) q3–6 months × 2 years, then q6 months to 5 years total
Colonoscopy at 1 year; if advanced adenoma repeat in 1 year, otherwise 3 years then every 5 years
dMMR on immunotherapy: re-evaluate q2–3 months; MSS metastatic being converted to resectable: q2 months

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: FOLFOXIRI is not recommended when resection is contraindicated after neoadjuvant therapy
Resection is preferred over ablation or SBRT for oligometastatic liver- or lung-only disease
Favorable pT3 N0 (well/moderately differentiated, <2 mm mesorectal invasion, no lymphovascular involvement, upper rectum) may go to surveillance rather than adjuvant therapy
pT1–3 N1 can be treated with FOLFOX or CAPEOX alone, without radiation
